ov: The Maldives has developed a high-end dining scene driven by luxury resorts, where international chefs run ambitious specialty restaurants. Much of the fine dining focuses on imported luxury ingredients alongside local seafood like yellowfin tuna and reef fish. Access requires staying at or visiting specific resort islands.
months: Resort dining rooms operate consistently, serving tasting menus that blend French, Japanese, and modern Asian techniques with Maldivian seafood. Underwater restaurants and overwater pavilions require advance booking, especially during the drier months when resort occupancy peaks.

ov: Singapore has a strong craft beer and cocktail scene, with local breweries and distilleries producing spirits infused with regional botanicals. Visitors can tour microbreweries or taste locally distilled gin and rum. Indoor taprooms and bars provide relief from the tropical heat.
months: Local microbreweries pour craft beers infused with tropical fruits and spices, while distilleries produce gin using Southeast Asian botanicals like calamansi and torch ginger. Taprooms and tasting rooms operate consistently, with flights and tours.
